text:
incident-bot: PAGED: sev2 latency-regression-prod — p95 spikes across prod-serving-a > 800ms, auto-alerting. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-regression :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: paging Mia (oncall) and oncall-sre. Escalation: 1st oncall (Mia) — please ack.
Mia (oncall): acked, looking. seeing p50 ~120ms (baseline ~40ms), p95 ~820ms (baseline ~210ms). Confirming impact: 15% of customer requests experiencing tails >500ms.
Aj: are we seeing any recent infra changes? kernel, scheduler, kubelets?
Sasha: I can pull traces — giving a quick flame for requests hitting inference-service/v2.
Sasha: Trace snippet from jaeger (streamlined):
```
service: inference-service
span: serve.forward  (avg 40ms -> 220ms), tail 900ms
span: kv-cache.lookup (p95 150ms -> 560ms)
span: gpu-inference.exec (unchanged)
```
Mia (oncall): interesting, gpu span is stable, CPU-bound spans and kv-cache lookups are blowing up. That points at host/kernel level or user-space io.
Kevin: I rolled out kernel-build-2026-03-12 to prod-serving-a nodes at 03:12 UTC last night (canary -> all). Are those nodes the same ones reporting spike?
Sasha: correlating node list... yes, >80% of affected requests came from nodes with kernel-build-2026-03-12.
sre-runner: adding to timeline below.
Mia (oncall): timeline (quick):
- 2026-03-12 03:12 UTC: kernel-build-2026-03-12 deployment to prod-serving-a (rolling)
- 2026-03-13 01:28 UTC: first customer alert (p95 bump observed)
- 2026-03-13 01:30 UTC: auto-alert -> current thread created
- 2026-03-13 01:34 UTC: tracing shows p95 hit on kv-cache.lookup and serve.forward
- 2026-03-13 01:40 UTC: hypothesis: kernel change -> started investigating
- 2026-03-13 01:55 UTC: rolled a 10-node canary rollback to kernel-build-2026-03-05 on subset

Aj: what do perf counters show on affected nodes vs rolled-back canary?
Sasha: grabbing perf stats (1-minute sample) from affected node vs canary node:
```
# affected node (kernel-2026-03-12)
cycles: 3.45e9
instructions: 9.2e8
cache-misses: 2.1e6
context-switches: 18,452
soft-irqs: 5,210
sched-switches: 25,100
syscall-latency-avg: 120us
syscall-latency-p95: 820us

# canary (kernel-2026-03-05)
cycles: 3.40e9
instructions: 9.1e8
cache-misses: 4.1e5
context-switches: 6,300
soft-irqs: 1,100
sched-switches: 8,520
syscall-latency-avg: 30us
syscall-latency-p95: 210us
```
Mia (oncall): huge difference in cache-misses and context-switches. Looks like kernel update increased context-switch rate and cache line churn.
Kevin: kernel changelog had a patch to the scheduler and a backported high-res timer tweak that changed tick handling; also enabled preempt_count tracking. Could be related.
Aj: alternative hypothesis: a user-space change in continuous-batching loop? any deploys to inference-service around the same time?
Sasha: service deploys: none since 02:00 UTC. Only infra/kernel change matches timeline.
Mia (oncall): Hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
- H1: kernel scheduler/timing change -> increased syscalls/context-switches -> p95 latency regression. (lead: Kevin)
- H2: kernel config accidentally enabled a debug/tracing flag -> extra overhead in syscalls. (lead: Aj)
- H3: NUMA balancing or late memory reclaim causing KV cache misses (lead: Sasha)

Mia (oncall): mitigation step 1: moved 10% of traffic off prod-serving-a to prod-serving-b via routing policy (traffic shift started at 01:58 UTC). Observed global p95 drop of ~30% but affected cluster still high.
Sasha: canary rollback (10 nodes) results: p95 on canary nodes dropped to ~230ms within 5 minutes after rollback. Aggregate p95 for cluster reduced from 820ms -> 420ms after traffic shift + canary rollback.
Aj: can we roll full rollback? risk assessment?
Kevin: rollback risk low for kernel, but needs node reboots and drain. Estimated 20m per node; we have autoscaling and spare capacity in other clusters. Recommend staged rollback across prod-serving-a in 3 waves.
Mia (oncall): starting wave 1 rollback of 30% nodes to kernel-2026-03-05 now. I'll coordinate with infra to drain nodes and move pods.
Mia (oncall): running drain command (example):
```
kubectl drain node/prod-a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
reboot node -> boot with kernel 2026-03-05 via image tag
kubectl uncordon node/prod-a-12
```
Sasha: metrics after wave1 (5 minutes post): cluster p95 -> 310ms, per-node p95 on rolled nodes -> 220ms, remaining nodes -> 740ms.
Mia (oncall): good, wave2 starting. keep monitoring for regressions.
pagerduty-bot: User impact: ~18% of sessions experienced >500ms latency during peak; currently reduced to ~6% after traffic shift + partial rollback.
Aj: can someone attach dmesg from affected node at time of spike? looking for RCU stalls or kernel error messages.
Kevin: dmesg snippet from affected node around 01:27 UTC:
```
[01:27:12] kernel: audit: type=1400 audit(1615658832.123:44): avc:  denied  { read } for  pid=1234 comm="kworker/3:1" name="somefile" dev="sda1" ino=12345 scontext=system_u:system_r:kernel_t:s0 tcontext=unconfined_u:object_r:var_t:s0 tclass=file
[01:27:14] kernel: perf: interrupt took too long (2500 us)
[01:27:15] kernel: WARNING: CPU: 3 PID: 0 at kernel/timekeeping/core.c:...
```
Sasha: we also have increased futex wait times in traces, likely due to scheduler preemption behaviour.
Mia (oncall): current status: partial rollback in progress, p95 trending down. Taking oncall handoff in 30m — Aj will take mid-shift and continue RCA.
Aj: noted, I'll take over at 02:28 UTC. Next steps: finish cluster rollback, validate p95 normalization for 30 minutes, run perf bench on both kernels, open postmortem doc and include timeline + perf counters + kernel diff.
Kevin: I'm going to prepare a minimal repro that stresses kv-cache.lookup under both kernels to measure context-switch and cache-miss rates.
Sasha: created temporary dashboards: /dashboards/latency-regression-1755556789 showing p50/p95 by kernel version and node tags.
Mia (oncall): customer comms: support-signal shows a handful of enterprise customers reported degraded performance; CS pinged and asked for ETA. Sending heads-up: We expect full rollback to complete within 90 minutes and will update status then.
incident-bot: Incident severity remains sev2. Documenting action items to postmortem doc: rollback timeline, perf outputs, kernel diff, owners.
Mia (oncall): final note before handoff: prioritise collecting perf.data on affected nodes (perf record -a -g -- sleep 60) and upload to s3://redwood-ops/incidents/1755556789/perf/. Aj, Sasha, Kevin assigned as owners.
Aj: taking over. will re-run end-to-end checks, ensure canary metrics are stable. :thumbsup:
Sasha: continuing traces + log aggregation; will attach full flamegraphs to postmortem.
Kevin: will draft RCA hypothesis section and include kernel patchset analysis.
Mia (oncall): thanks all. handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
